in_urdu.name: نزہت
in_urdu.long_meaning: نزہت ایک ایسا نام ہے جو عربی زبان کے الفعل 'نزھ' سے ماخوذ ہے، جس کا مطلب ہے دور ہونا یا آرام کرنا۔ یہ نام خوشی، سکون اور دل کی آرام کی حالت کو ظاہر کرتا ہے۔ جنوبی ایشیائی مسلمانوں کی روایت میں، یہ نام روحانی سکون اور اندرونی سکھ کے لئے قدرتی جمال سے وابستہ ہے۔

in_pashto.name: نزہت
in_pashto.meaning: آرام، خوشی، او د ژوند ښکلا
in_pashto.long_meaning: نزہت داسې یو نوم دی چی د ارام او خوشی معنی لري. دا نوم د افغان او پښتون دودیزو ارزښتونو سره تړلی دی او د ژوند ښکلا او خوندیتوب څرګندوي. په پښتو کلتور کې، دا نوم د روحاني سولې او اندروني خوشحالي لپاره کارول کېږي.

in_english.name: Nuzhatun
in_english.meaning: delight, pleasure, enjoyment of nature and life
in_english.long_meaning: Nuzhatun is a name derived from the Arabic root 'n-z-h', which means to distance oneself from harm or difficulty. The name signifies enjoyment, pleasure, and delight in nature and life. It has Quranic roots and connotations of spiritual and psychological well-being. Historically, the name has been used across various Muslim cultures, symbolizing happiness, serenity, and a deep appreciation for life's beauty.

data.cultural_impact: The name "Nuzhatun" is of Arabic origin, found in various Islamic contexts, often used for both humans and animals. The name is beautiful and the meaning of delight and pleasure can be associated with various aspects of Islamic culture. For instance, it can be linked to the art of calligraphy, where the intricacy and beauty of the letters bring joy and delight to those who appreciate it. It can also be associated with the joy and happiness that comes from serving Allah and living an Islamic lifestyle. In Islamic sacred literatures, the term "nuzhat" is used to describe the joy and pleasure experienced by angels in serving Allah, which is a concept that can inspire and motivate Muslims to strive for their own delight and joy in following the teachings of Islam.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Nuzhatun" can be seen as a reminder of the joy and pleasure that comes from serving Allah and living according to His guidance. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "The most beloved to me and the closest to me in the Garden are those who have the most fear from Allah and the most love for Him, and who have the most skins burnt (through striving in His way) and many wounds in His cause." (Bukhari and Muslim). In this context, the name "Nuzhatun" can be seen as a reflection of the inner joy and happiness that comes from pleasing Allah and striving for His pleasure. It can also be seen as a reminder to focus on the blessings and joys of this world that come from following the path of righteousness, rather than the temporary pleasures of this world that can lead to spiritual decline and despair. Ultimately, the name "Nuzhatun" serves as a reminder to seek the everlasting delight and pleasure of paradise by living a righteous and obedient life in accordance with the teachings of Islam.
